content: Certain infections you have previously experienced may reactivate, potentially causing the return of disease symptoms. Additionally, symptoms may arise if your immune system becomes overactive. This immune response can occur at any time, either shortly after initiating HIV treatment or even months later. While taking this medication, changes in body fat distribution may occur. These changes can include increased fat in areas such as the upper back and abdomen, and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The exact cause and long-term effects of these changes remain unknown. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, etravirine commonly causes a mild rash, which typically appears during the second week of treatment and resolves within one to two weeks. It may be difficult to distinguish this mild rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, also contact your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before starting etravirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Your doctor may need to adjust your treatment or monitor you more closely if you are taking certain combinations of HIV medications. Other medications can affect how etravirine is removed from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. Examples include macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin and clarithromycin) and rifamycins (such as rifabutin, rifampin, and rifapentine). Etravirine itself can also influence the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect their function. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: Regular lab and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, should be conducted while taking this medication. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it after a meal as soon as you remember. If more than six hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. For further details, contact your healthcare provider or pharmacist.
